steps.title: Gather consumables and equipment
steps.instruction: Collect the following consumables: Droplet Generation Oil (Catalog: 1863005), ddPCR™ Droplet Reader Oil (Catalog: 1863004), DG8™ Cartridges (Catalog: 1864008), DG8™ Gaskets (Catalog: 1863009), 96‑well plates (Catalog: 12001925). Also have the QX200™ Droplet Generator, PX1 PCR Plate Sealer, vortex, centrifuge, and QX200™ Droplet Reader ready.

steps.title: Label microtubes
steps.instruction: Label each microtube clearly and set them aside for preparation of the reaction mix.

steps.title: Prepare reaction mix
steps.instruction: Assemble the reaction components according to Table 1: add 10 µl of 2× ddPCR Supermix for Probes (final concentration 1×) per reaction. Dispense equal aliquots of this master mix into each labeled tube. Finally, add the DNA sample to each reaction tube as the last step.

steps.title: Mix and centrifuge tubes
steps.instruction: Gently mix the DNA samples and reagents on the vortex until homogeneous, then briefly centrifuge the tubes to collect liquid at the bottom.

steps.title: Load cartridge with mix and oil
steps.instruction: Load 20 µl of each prepared reaction mix into a sample well of a DG8™ Cartridge for the QX200™ Droplet Generator. Add 70 µl of Droplet Generation Oil into the corresponding oil wells. If using the Automated Droplet Generator, follow its instruction manual.

steps.title: Generate droplets and transfer
steps.instruction: After droplet generation with the QX200™ Droplet Generator, carefully transfer the droplets into a clean 96‑well plate and seal the plate with the PX1 PCR Plate Sealer.

steps.title: Thermal cycle droplets
steps.instruction:
Place the sealed plate in a thermal cycler and run the program (Table 2):
- Enzyme activation: 95 °C for 10 min, ramp 2 °C/sec, 1 cycle
- Denaturation: 94 °C for 30 s, ramp 2 °C/sec, 40 cycles
- Annealing/extension: 60 °C for 60 s, ramp 2 °C/sec, 40 cycles
- Enzyme deactivation: 98 °C for 5 min, ramp 2 °C/sec, 1 cycle.

steps.title: Read droplets in reader
steps.instruction: After thermal cycling, place the sealed 96‑well plate in the QX200™ Droplet Reader and acquire fluorescence data.

steps.title: Set thresholds and interpret
steps.instruction: Manually set fluorescence thresholds (RLEP = 5000, groEL = 2500). Define a positive well as having more than 4 fluorescent events above the threshold. The test sample is considered positive when at least 3 of the 4 duplicate wells (RLEP and groEL) are positive.
